_about: One plain sentence per design-system term, for people who are not designers (Intake section 0, Plain words). The dashboard shows it as a tooltip wherever the term appears in a question or option. Add a term here when a question starts using it.

terms.Design system: The shared kit of colors, text styles, spacing and ready-made parts that every screen is built from.
terms.DS: Short for design system: the shared kit of colors, text styles, spacing and parts every screen is built from.
terms.Primitives: The raw values: every color shade, size and number the design system may use.
terms.Semantic: Named roles such as 'page background' or 'error text' that point to a raw value, so Light and Dark can differ.
terms.Semantics: Named roles such as 'page background' or 'error text' that point to a raw value, so Light and Dark can differ.
terms.Variables: Named values stored in Figma (colors, sizes) that parts use instead of typed numbers, so one change updates everything.
terms.Tokens: The design system's named values (colors, sizes, fonts) shared by Figma and the code.
terms.Token: A named value of the design system (a color, a size, a font) shared by Figma and the code.
terms.Component: A reusable part, such as a button or an input, that screens use as copies.
terms.Components: Reusable parts, such as buttons and inputs, that screens use as copies.
terms.Variant: One version of a part, for example a small or a disabled button.
terms.Variants: The versions of a part, for example small, large or disabled buttons.
terms.Atoms: The smallest parts, such as a button, a checkbox or an icon.
terms.Molecules: Parts made of a few smaller parts, such as an input with its label.
terms.Organisms: Bigger blocks made of parts, such as a top bar or a card.
terms.Patterns: Page-level layouts, such as a sign-up form or a list page.
terms.Greenfield: A new product: nothing has been designed yet.
terms.Brownfield: Something already exists in Figma: screens, a design system, or both.
terms.Code to Design: A coded app (for example a GitHub repo) is the source, and its screens are drawn in Figma.
terms.Scenario C: Cleaning up an existing design system and the screens that use it.
terms.Scenario D: Code to Design: drawing a coded app's screens in Figma.
terms.Checkpoint: A stop where you look at the result and approve it before the next phase starts.
terms.Foundation: The base of the design system: colors, text styles, spacing, corners and icons.
terms.Light and Dark: Two color modes: the same screens with a light or a dark background.
terms.RTL: Right to left: layouts that read from the right, for Arabic.
terms.Storybook: A website where developers can see and try every part of the design system.
terms.Publish: Make the design system available to your other Figma files (Assets > Library > Publish).
terms.Accept updates: In a screens file, take the newest version of the published design system.
terms.Library: A Figma file whose parts and styles other files can use.
terms.Auto Layout: Figma's way to make a frame resize and space its content by itself.
terms.Yolo: FigCli's fast mode: Figma is set up once so Claude can work in it without a plugin.
terms.FigCli: A small tool that lets Claude read and change your open Figma files.
terms.Desktop Bridge: A Figma plugin that lets Claude read and change the open file.
terms.Fix on create: Problems found in a copied file are fixed right away in your copy, never in the original.
terms.Gap table: A list of the parts a set of screens needs, with the ones still missing.
terms.Flow map: Every screen and step of one task, such as signing up, drawn before the screens are built.
terms.Variable Map: A table of every variable in an existing file: what it is for and where it is used.
terms.Reference template: A studied design system from the library, used as the starting structure.
terms.Audit: An automatic check that every screen and part uses the design system correctly.
terms.Fidelity: How closely the Figma screen matches its source, measured in pixels and values.
terms.Intake: The first questions about the project, asked one at a time.
terms.Inputs: Your files for the project: brand, inspiration, screenshots and research.
terms.Brand Foundation: One small file with the brand colors and fonts that the iOS and Android systems copy from.
terms.Mobile Adaptive: One Figma file for iOS and Android, where a switch shows each platform's own look.
terms.Material 3: Google's design rules for Android apps.
terms.Apple HIG: Apple's design rules for iPhone and iPad apps.
terms.Slot: A space inside a part where you can put any content.
terms.Instance: A copy of a part placed on a screen; it updates when the part changes.
